title: Certificates of Deposit: the penalty days the charter fixes, for checking a booked penalty
content:
## Scope

When an early withdrawal penalty on a Certificates of Deposit certificate is checked for having been booked at the wrong number of penalty days, this rule gives the number of days the charter fixes, against which the booked penalty days are compared.

## Rule

The charter penalty days are the tier's standard penalty days, except that when the penalty posted no more than six calendar days after the term start date they are the greater of the tier's standard penalty days and the tier's first-six-days minimum penalty days.

## How the six days are counted

- The anchor is the term start date on the certificate; the date compared is the posted date of the penalty.
- The number of calendar days from the term start date to the penalty's posted date is taken.
- Six days or fewer: the greater of the two figures applies. Seven days or more: the standard penalty days apply.

## Boundary cases (illustrative figures, not tier values)

Assume a tier with standard penalty days of 0 and a first-six-days minimum of 5, and a term start date of 1 May.

| Penalty posted on | Calendar days after the term start date | Charter penalty days |
|---|---|---|
| 5 May | 4 | 5, the greater of 0 and 5 |
| 7 May | 6 | 5, the greater of 0 and 5 |
| 8 May | 7 | 0, the standard days |

With a tier whose standard penalty days are 60 and whose minimum is 5, a penalty posted 3 May has charter penalty days of 60, since 60 is the greater.

## Points of judgement

**A penalty posted on the sixth calendar day after the term start date. Standard days or the greater figure?**
The greater figure: the exception covers a penalty posted no more than six calendar days after the term start date, and six is not more than six.

**Does the exception depend on the tier?**
No. The comparison with the first-six-days minimum applies on every tier; only the figures differ by tier.
